build.system: pip (setuptools via pyproject.toml; pure Python, nothing compiles; the package 'tmm' is mapped onto the repository root)
commands: python3.12 -m venv venv-tmm && venv-tmm/bin/pip install numpy scipy matplotlib   # numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, matplotlib 3.11.2 on Python 3.12.3
SRC=<scratch copy of the checkout, directory named tmm>
python -m pip install --no-deps --target $SITE $SRC   # SRC = the scratch copy of the checkout, SITE = an empty target directory; 3.8 s wall, build isolation on
PKG=<a directory holding a symlink named tmm to the checkout>   # the alternative: the checkout itself as the package directory on PYTHONPATH; identical test output
pitfalls: pip install --no-build-isolation fails in a bare Python 3.12 venv with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'setuptools' (venv no longer seeds setuptools); use the default build isolation or pip install setuptools first

the package is flat: pyproject.toml maps package 'tmm' to '.', so the checkout directory must be named tmm (or symlinked as such) to be importable without installing; the vendored tree under code/tmm/ has the right name by construction

landscape.how_to_run: python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.run_all()"   (no pytest, no assertions: each test prints difference fractions that should be zero within rounding)
landscape.notes: basic_test and position_resolved_test embed reference values from the author's earlier Mathematica program; the other six compare against physical identities (energy conservation, Poynting continuity, R+T=1, analytic vs numeric absorption, coherent vs incoherent averaging, overflow protection). Exit status is 0 whatever the numbers.

landscape.how_to_run: python -c "import tmm.examples as ex; ex.sample1()"  (each sample builds a Matplotlib figure and calls plt.show(); sample5 also prints rgb and xyY)
landscape.notes: sample3 reproduces Handbook of Ellipsometry (Tompkins 2005) Fig. 1.14, sample6 reproduces Mater. Trans. 51 (2010) 1150 Fig. 6a, sample5 compares against a published SiO2-on-Si colour chart; no numbers ship. sample5 needs colorpy.
the six samples of examples.py pasted into notebook cells with their rendered plots; same code paths, deduplicated to examples.py

landscape.how_to_run: not runnable (documentation; manual_source/manual.lyx is its LyX source)
landscape.notes: the user manual; physics derivations are in arXiv:1603.02720

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$SITE MPLBACKEND=Agg python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.run_all()"
runs.reproduced: yes: 15 digits (basic_test and position_resolved_test against the embedded Mathematica values, largest difference fraction 1.0e-15; the identities hold to 1e-16)
outputs: stdout: 89 text lines of difference fractions and printed arrays
runs.nondeterminism: none seen: stdout byte-identical across two runs, and identical between the pip-installed package and the checkout on PYTHONPATH
pitfalls: nothing asserts and the exit status is always 0: a check must recompute the graded quantities itself, never parse pass/fail
the opacity warning is printed once per process through a module global, so stdout depends on which tests ran earlier in the same process; grade numbers, never the text

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.basic_test()"
runs.reproduced: yes: 15 digits (r, t, R, T for s and p, psi and Delta against Mathematica; largest difference fraction 1.0e-15 on t_s, Delta 6.5e-14 because Delta itself is 2.1e-3)

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.position_resolved_test()"
runs.reproduced: yes: 15 digits (kz, Poynting vector and absorption at one depth against Mathematica, 2e-16 to 4e-16); absorption sums to 1 exactly; Poynting continuity and end-point identities at 1e-16; the finite-difference derivative check lands at 4.6e-12 (p) and 3.9e-11 (s), the O(h) stencil error, not a fault

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.position_resolved_test2()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identities only): absorption sums to 1 exactly with complex incident and final media; continuity and end-point identities at 1e-16; finite difference at 5e-11

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.absorp_analytic_fn_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identities only): the analytic absorption function equals position_resolved to 0 and 1.7e-16, and its flipped copy agrees from the other side

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.incoherent_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identities only): inc_tmm against the closed-form three-layer sums and against coh_tmm at 1e-16 or exactly 0; the thickness-averaged (357 thicknesses) and wavelength-averaged (234 wavelengths) coherent runs agree with the incoherent result to 1.5e-5 to 8e-5, the finite-sample residual of the averaging, printed as 'discrepancy'
outputs: stdout: 14 difference fractions, 4 discrepancy lines, two 2x4 arrays
pitfalls: the 'discrepancy' lines are 1e-5 by design (finite averaging), not failures; a check grades the computed values, not their closeness to zero

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.RT_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identities only): R+T=1 at a single interface to 4.4e-16, power_entering equals T to 3.5e-16

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.coh_overflow_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identity only): the vw_list of the five-layer stack with a layer of imag(delta)=18850 agrees with the truncated three-layer stack in its first entries (printed, compared by eye: 0.6066665-0.1116073j both)
outputs: stdout: the opacity warning once, two printed complex arrays
pitfalls: imag(delta) > 35 is clamped to 35 in coh_tmm and a warning is printed once per process; amplitudes behind the opaque layer come out at 1e-16 to 1e-32, so a pointwise bound on vw_list needs an absolute term

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.inc_overflow_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identity only): power_entering_list of the five-layer stack agrees with the three-layer stack in its first entries (0.4210526315789473 both)
outputs: stdout: two printed lists; under numpy 2 the entries print as np.float64(...)
pitfalls: single-pass transmission P < 1e-30 is floored to 1e-30 in inc_tmm, which sets the 1.97e-30 entries behind the opaque layer; the printed list format depends on the numpy major version, so grade numbers, not text

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG MPLBACKEND=Agg python -c "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt; plt.show=lambda *a,**k: None; import tmm.examples as ex; ex.sample1()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (a plot): reflection versus wavenumber, 400 points, normal incidence and 45-degree unpolarised; 1200 coh_tmm calls
pitfalls: every sample ends in plt.show(), which blocks under an interactive backend; run with MPLBACKEND=Agg and a stubbed plt.show
Python 3.12 prints SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence '\c' for the '$^\circ$' titles; harmless

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG MPLBACKEND=Agg python -c "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt; plt.show=lambda *a,**k: None; import tmm.examples as ex; ex.sample2()"

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG MPLBACKEND=Agg python -c "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt; plt.show=lambda *a,**k: None; import tmm.examples as ex; ex.sample4()"

temp_plot.png written twice into the working directory by colorpy.plots.spectrum_plot

the irgb values are gamma-corrected integers 0-255, a discrete output; the linear rgb and xyY are the continuous quantities

runs.reason_not_run: its code cells are the six samples of examples.py pasted with their plots; the same code paths were run through examples.py

pitfalls.symptom: pip install --no-build-isolation: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'setuptools'
pitfalls.workaround: let pip build in isolation (it fetches setuptools) or pip install setuptools first; or skip installing and put a directory named tmm on PYTHONPATH

pitfalls.symptom: the tests print difference fractions and always exit 0; nothing asserts
pitfalls.workaround: a check recomputes the graded quantities (r, t, R, T, psi, Delta, kz, Poynting, absorption, vw_list, power_entering) and grades those; the printed text is never the observable

pitfalls.symptom: stdout differs between processes depending on whether coh_overflow_test ran first (the opacity warning is printed once per process via a module global) and on the numpy major version (np.float64(...) reprs)
pitfalls.workaround: grade numbers written to files, not stdout

pitfalls.symptom: plt.show() blocks under an interactive backend
pitfalls.workaround: MPLBACKEND=Agg and stub plt.show (or save figures instead)

pitfalls.symptom: PyPI colorpy 0.1.1 fails to import on Python 3 (No module named 'colormodels')
pitfalls.workaround: pip install the fish2000 ColorPy fork from GitHub at commit 4c9e5b2e334851b42626f9a1eda31197739b097e (github.com/fish2000/ColorPy) (LGPL-3.0); then examples.colors_were_imported is True and sample5 runs in 8.4 s

pitfalls.symptom: temp_plot.png appears in the working directory
pitfalls.workaround: run in a scratch cwd; colorpy.plots.spectrum_plot saves its figure unconditionally

pitfalls.symptom: Python 3.12 SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence '\c' when examples.py is compiled
pitfalls.workaround: harmless; comes from '$^\circ$' in plot titles

pitfalls.symptom: is_forward_angle decides the forward wave by comparing imag(n cos theta) with 100*EPSILON, and coh_tmm clamps imag(delta) > 35 while inc_tmm floors P < 1e-30
pitfalls.workaround: discrete choices in the source; the official decks sit far from the thresholds (imag(delta)=18850 in the overflow tests), which a rubric warrant should say

not_run.why: the same six samples as examples.py; running the .py exercised every code path the notebook holds
